Posted April 8, 2006  
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
 What Is More Important, Prohibition Or The Patients? The Death of Cheryl Miller Should Remind Us All To Demand A Change In Priorities. Should Pain Be A Crime?

A week ago today, I went to Portland to speak to the Oregon Green Free medical cannabis patients group. Steve Tuck had told me about this remarkable group whose website has created both a real and virtual community of patients. They help themselves by helping others.

(It was also great to see my old friend, Sandee Burbank of MAMAS.org. MAMAS is one of the few real drug education programs in America, but is largely ignored by both sides of the drugwar debate.)

There were more than one hundred patients there and I tried to convey to them how far the medical marijuana movement has come since NORML organized what we optimistically called the First National Medical Marijuana Day in 1994. We were completely ignored by the DC/national media, even though we held a press conference with distinguished speakers at the National Press Club and had a group of patients, some in wheelchairs, picketing the White House. 

Two years later, in 1996, Prop 215 would shock the Establishment, especially the DC/national media, because they could not imagine the people actually doing something without their approval.

Two years later, Portland's Oregonian newspaper would lie to its readers in an unsuccessful effort to try to block medical cannabis in the first state to decriminalize marijuana possession back in the 1970s.


See
The Portland Oregonian Escalates Its Propaganda Campaign Against Medical Marijuana Initiative  

Yes, we have come a long way, but after all these years, there is still a struggle between man's compassionate and predatory natures. In that room I could see that compassion is slowly winning, but I also continued to hear stories about the predators, the narks, of course, but also the black market growers and rip-off artists who are the dark side of our side.

One frequently heard complaint was that MPP continues to use Peter Lewis money to exploit the patients to get Rob Kampia's picture in the paper for measures that may actually harm patients.
See
 MPP Incompetence Continues to Embarrass Marijuana Movement. Bad Initiative Dead In Nevada for Wrong Reasons. Good Initiative in Arkansas Abandoned. Local Activists Persevere.

Just as there is a symbiotic relationship between the narks and organized crime, there are pseudo-activists, political consultants, organized quacks and other predators pretending to be compassionate, who use the patients for their on careerism and/or ego gratification. 

Consequently, my message to the Oregon patients was simply that they must continue to take charge of their own lives and not look to others to help them. (Does that include me? Yes, it includes everyone.)
See
 Have The Sick And Dying Liberated Alberta Yet?
No, But They Are Working On It. 

A few days later, I was watching the news and our beloved President was speaking about empowering patients. Fortunately, I have access to a very effective anti-emetic. Nonetheless, George Bush and I were saying essentially the same thing in very different contexts with radically different meanings. Orwell talked about depriving words of their meaning.
See
 Drug Czar Conducts War On Meaning In Washington Post
and
From The Drug Czar's 8-Year Plan to the Republican's Drug-Free Century Act,
The Prohibitionist Agenda Is War Without End. Orwell Would Understand.
Analysis By Richard Cowan 

While we have indeed made a lot of progress, my other point to the patients was simply that medical marijuana laws are really just loopholes in bad laws, and are written more for the purpose of maintaining prohibition than for helping the patients.

As noted, part of the fault lies with political opportunism, and the recalcitrance of the narks, but as Dr. Lester Grinspoon concluded in Marihuana, the Forbidden Medicine, cannabis can only be used to its full medical potential when it is fully legal and removed from the control of a medical establishment that it fundamentally hostile to it and invincibly ignorant about it.
See
 Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

While getting the patients off the battlefields of the drugwar is morally necessary, and I have never had a problem supporting any medical cannabis law that would work for a significant number of patients, the fact remains that medical marijuana  laws are bad laws. See
 People Who Live In Pain Should Not Have to Live In Fear. In Santa Cruz, Celebrating Freedom and Denouncing A Murder.  

They do nothing for millions of patients in the US and hundreds of millions of poor people in poor counties around the world where a medical loophole is completely unworkable.

I will always stand up for my friends, but I really cannot argue that an American has more of a right to medical cannabis than sick person in Mexico or Africa, who may need it even more.
See
 World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Also, the absurdity of fighting for the smallest loophole was made clear by the latest round of the Raich cases, which is now before the 9th Circuit, on its way back to the Supreme Court.  

The effort to get the Courts to allow patients to grow their own medicine foundered on a broad interpretation of the Interstate Commerce clause and the regulation of wheat cultivation, having nothing to do with the medical value of cannabis or the needs of patients.
See
Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report June 6, 2005 Supreme Court: 6 To 3 Against Patients Right To Grow. Rehnquist, Thomas Dissent Political Victory. State Laws Unaffected.   

Now we are reduced to arguing that patients should be allowed to have cannabis if their lives really, really, really depend on it. That is too much like my definition of what I call the moderate prohibitionist position on medical marijuana last rites and a joint. The patient can have toke, but has to promise to die ASAP.

Of course, even that would be too much for George Empower the Patients Bush.

In the 9th Circuit, Judge Harry Pregerson asked Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Quinlivan whether it was alright for Raich to die or endure unbearable suffering.

So go ahead and die. That would be all right? he asked.

Congress has made that value judgment, Quinlivan responded.

In fact, Congress has made no such value judgment. When politicians respond to letters from constituents about medical cannabis, they never say that sick people should suffer and die.

Instead, the politicians hide behind the prohibitionist ideology that claims,  Marijuana is a Dangerous and Addictive Drug And Should Not be Legalized for Medicinal Use.
See
 The Congressional Record On The House Medical Marijuana Debate
Requires Powerful Anti-Emetics
and
 Documenting DEA Lies About Medical Cannabis Ruling: High Court Upholds Marijuana As Dangerous Drug. But the Court Did Nothing of the Sort.  

That is beginning to change, and more and more are discovering that medical marijuana and even the legalization of cannabis is not quite as controversial as the media pretend.
See
 Leakin Bout My G-G-Generation. Leak of AARP Poll On Medical Cannabis Assures Story Will Have Long Legs. Mainstreaming Real Threat To Prohibitionist Party Line.  
And from NORML See
 Zogby Poll: Nearly Half Of Americans Believe Pot Should Be Regulated Like Alcohol - Majorities In The East And West Coasts Back Legalization 

Quinlivan argued that no one has a right to use marijuana, even to save their lives, because a ruling in Raich's favor would open the floodgates to people who want to use other substances that are not approved for medical purposes. In other words, Americans must be prepared to suffer and die for prohibition. Certainly, a lot of them already have.


See
 The Murder of Steve McWilliams An Indictment, Not An Obituary. The Absurdity of Evil. Condolences from NORML.  

Of course, I hope that Raich is successful, but I find it increasingly difficult to be enthusiastic about ever-narrower loopholes. The paradox for patients is that ultimately only legalization will work. At the upcoming NORML conference in San Francisco a great deal of time will be devoted to the medical aspect of the issue, for obvious reasons. Nonetheless, we should not measure our freedom by the length of our leashes. Ultimately, we own our own bodies and souls or we are the property of the state. There are no loopholes in that ultimate truth.
